messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1782109876 - region-us-west-2 runtime queue pressure - p95 queue length > 500

maria: picking this up. Dashboard shows a fast rise in queued requests and continuous_batching queueing. p50 ok, tails blown out.

aj: any 5xxs or customer-facing errors?

maria: mostly 429s for bursty tenants and a small uptick in deadline-exceeded in some clients. No big 500 spike.

maria: quick metrics snapshot:
```
- total_reqs/s: 14.8k (sustained burst for 12m)
- avg_batch_size: 6.2 (down from usual 10)
- qlen p95: 540 (baseline < 80)
- p99 latency: 2.1s (baseline ~650ms)
- gpu_mem avg: 82% but some hosts hitting 94%
```

tom: we shipped packing-v2 yesterday which changed token packing heuristics; could be causing more small batches and queue pressure.

maria: prefer mitigate live rather than rollback. We have these runtime knobs: continuous_batching.max_wait_ms, continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens, per-tenant token_rate_limit, stream_enabled_by_tier.

chandra: what mitigations are safe to flip without code deploy?

maria: we can: 1) apply temporary per-tenant token caps for offending tenants, 2) globally increase max_wait_ms to allow more packing (trade latency for throughput), 3) increase max_batch_tokens for CPU-heavy models only, and 4) toggle streaming for low-priority tiers.

aj: note that increasing max_wait_ms will raise interactive tail latency but reduces 429s. We should scope changes to model-tags where possible.

maria: proposed immediate plan:
- throttle top-6 bursty tenants to 0.7x their short-term allowance
- bump continuous_batching.max_wait_ms from 15 -> 80ms globally for 15m window
- set continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens 1536 -> 3072 but only for model-tag:encoder-heavy
- disable response streaming for tier:free and tier:trial

maria: applying changes now via admin API:
```bash
# throttle top tenants
curl -s -X POST https://admin.runtime.redwood/api/v1/rate-limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"tenants","ids":["fastlane","acme","bigdata","alpha-test","sandbox","trialcorp"],"multiplier":0.7}'

# bump batching wait and batch tokens (scoped by tag)
curl -s -X POST https://admin.runtime.redwood/api/v1/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching":{"max_wait_ms":80,"per_model_tags":{"encoder-heavy":{"max_batch_tokens":3072}}}}'

# toggle streaming off for low tiers
curl -s -X POST https://admin.runtime.redwood/api/v1/feature_flags \
  -d '{"feature":"streaming","scope":{"tiers":["free","trial"]},"enabled":false}'
```

deploy-bot: config-change accepted, job cfg-1782109876-1 queued. feature flag job ff-1782109876-1 applied.

sre-bot: warning: increasing max_wait_ms to 80ms may add ~200-900ms to p99 depending on sequence lengths. Suppressing redundant alerts for 12m.

maria: config job finished. checking effects...

sre-bot: post-change metrics:
```
- qlen p95 -> 160 (was 540)
- inflight -> 55 (was 120)
- p95 latency -> 560ms (was 1.2s)
- p99 latency -> 1.3s (was 2.1s)
- 429 rate -> 8/min (was 140/min)
- overall throughput -> +10% during mitigation window
```

aj: looks like it opened the queues but cleared backlog. p99 still elevated vs baseline but far fewer 429s.

cs-rep: pinged affected CSMs. Acme noticed a small interactive slowdown in dashboard queries but no errors. Fastlane flagged their app team; they accepted temporary cap.

maria: I'm going to monitor for 20m and then either 1) reduce max_wait_ms to a per-model scope, or 2) roll back and try stricter per-tenant caps if tail stays bad.

chandra: taking over for a 45m watch. maria, add mitigation summary to incident tracker and note change ids.

maria: done. summary note in incident ticket: cfg-1782109876-1, ff-1782109876-1. Mitigations: per-tenant multiplier 0.7 on six tenants, max_wait_ms 80ms global for 15m, per-model batch_tokens increased for encoder-heavy to 3072, streaming disabled for free/trial tiers. Observed: queue decreased ~70%, 429s drastically reduced, p99 increased to ~1.3s.

aj: action items post-mitigation:
- run perf sweep against packing-v2 to see packing distribution and why average batch size dropped
- add a runtime flag to set max_wait_ms per-model so we can target by model without global latency impact
- add telemetry that tags batch_size -> tenant_id to help attribution

maria: filed follow-ups and assigned to tom and aj for perf sweep.

tom: starting distributed perf job to reproduce 20k sustained req/s with packing-v2 to capture batch-size histogram and tokenization timing.

chandra: if we see queue creep >250 for >4 minutes or gpu_mem >93% we'll revert max_wait_ms to 15ms and apply stricter per-tenant throttles.

maria: noted. handoff complete. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident state changed to MITIGATED (runtime queue pressure) at 1782109999.

maria: end of thread.
